items.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025
items.q: I played pretty well when I was 14, like I could play, if I could play like Bunny Berigan, I could play “I Can’t Get Started,”

ctx.x: Sometimes this is hard to remember, but in your lengthy career, can you recall — I’m going to use a couple of adjectives here. The most bizarre gig, the worst gig, the kind of gig you come home and tell your wife, you go, “You can’t believe what happened on this one.”

Most of them are — some of them are funny you know. Like one of them was the most depressing job for me personally okay? I get called, once again somebody was sick. It was in Rochester when I was a student. Somebody is sick and this guy calls up and says, “Can you come and play over at the 50 Acres” which was the big barn-like place you know what I mean? And they had weddings and different kinds of things, just like the first job I ever played. And so I showed up and the guy that was running the job, he was about…

the ones that I did know I could really play. And then of course I could play solos when he wanted me to play a solo, but I couldn’t play the melody ever. I’d say just — but you know I’d listen and then I sort of sometimes I could play like a part of the melody because I figured it out just like I did the first job. I used the same technique. And then Joe Benedetto, he was sitting right next to me. The saxophone player? He says he knew what was going on and he said to me, “Vince, I have only known two or three…
